solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stop Republican interrupting judge

indicators.note: someone interrupting cuts into the middle of things, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: beak is British slang for a magistrate or judge
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A call to halt a Republican who keeps cutting in on a judge in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Beak is old British slang for a magistrate, the kind of judge who hears minor cases.
explanation.definitionFit: To break is to pause or halt an activity, a straightforward synonym for stop.

clue.text: Crow about French XI, second in league for period

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps around the next

parts.note: to crow is to boast, brag
onze is French for eleven

indicators.note: second in points to the second letter of the following word

parts.note: the second letter of league

explanation.surface: Boasting about the French football eleven, second in the league for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: XI is Roman eleven, the usual way of writing a football team, so French XI wants the French number.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bronze Age is the prehistoric era when bronze tools were made, so a period of history.

clue.text: News boss engaging people to perform his work?

indicators.note: to engage people is to take them on, so the word holds the other inside it

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper
men are people

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor hiring staff to do his job for him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the editor of the wordplay: the question mark flags that his work is correcting copy.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor's job is to correct and improve text, which is to emend it.

clue.text: Brown keeps on about cloth used up for jumper

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters are reversed
keeping something means holding it within, so the rest goes inside

parts.note: oak is a brown wood colour
taken as written
a rag is a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A man called Brown keeps going on about using up cloth to knit a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested containers, then the whole is read bottom to top. 'Jumper' is the British word for a sweater in the surface, but an animal that jumps here.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo moves by hopping on powerful hind legs, so it is a jumper in the literal sense.

clue.text: Heard not many resettled, renouncing right to be cleansed

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the sound of the next idea rather than its spelling

parts.note: few means not many; said aloud it matches the opening syllable

indicators.note: renouncing means giving something up, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: people who have resettled have migrated
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A report that a small group of migrants gave up their rights in order to be purified.
explanation.walkthrough: FU sounds like FEW, then MIGRATED loses its R to give FUMIGATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Fumigating disinfects a place with smoke or gas, so something fumigated has been cleansed.

clue.text: Stick-in-the-mud vaguely remembered losing a grand

indicators.note: losing something means it goes missing, so a letter drops out

parts.note: a foggy memory is a vague one
G stands for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: An old stick-in-the-mud only vaguely recalls losing a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: FOGGY loses one G.
explanation.definitionFit: A fogy (or fogey) is an old-fashioned, conservative person, the same idea as a stick-in-the-mud.

clue.text: Permit Oslo or Rome to slip badly as main city

indicators.note: badly means done wrongly, so both letter groups are set in a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Allowing either Oslo or Rome to decline badly as a leading city.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual double wordplay: 'Rome to slip' is also an anagram of the answer, and 'badly' serves both, so 'or' offers a second route to the same city.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is a country's chief or capital city, the main city of a region.

clue.text: Tail of calling bird, firmly fixed in the mind?

indicators.note: the tail is the back end, so the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the final letter of calling
a raven is a large black bird

explanation.surface: The end of a bird's call, firmly stuck in one's memory.
explanation.walkthrough: Graven literally means carved; 'graven on the memory' is the idiom the question mark points to.
explanation.definitionFit: Graven means engraved, and something engraved on the memory is indelibly fixed there.

clue.text: Follow match in clothing worn for exercise

parts.note: to track someone is to follow them
to suit is to match or go with

explanation.surface: Following a game while dressed in sports clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracksuit is a loose jacket and trousers worn for athletics training and exercise.

clue.text: Flood runs through at lower level

indicators.note: running through something means passing inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: down means lower
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A flood pours through on the floor below.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown land or a crop is to flood it completely under water.

clue.text: Suddenly close being seen in public

indicators.note: something seen in a place is located within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: overt means done openly, in public
nigh means near or close

explanation.surface: Someone close to a person suddenly being spotted out in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close being seen in public' looks like one phrase about a celebrity, but close is the inner piece and public the outer.
explanation.definitionFit: An overnight success happens all at once, so overnight is an adverb meaning suddenly or very quickly.

clue.text: Recalling battlefield doctor for mission?

parts.note: à la means in the style of, so recalling something
MO is a medical officer, the army's doctor

explanation.surface: Remembering a military medic who was sent out on a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alamo in Texas was a Spanish mission before its famous siege, and the question mark flags the definition by example; 'Remember the Alamo' makes 'Recalling' doubly sly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was originally a Franciscan mission church in San Antonio, so it is an example of a mission.

clue.text: Round about twelve houses?

indicators.note: to go round is to turn back the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: ca, from circa, means about
twelve is one dozen, written 1 DOZ with the 1 as I

explanation.surface: A vague estimate of a dozen homes, or a circular chart of twelve houses.
explanation.walkthrough: CA then I DOZ, all read backwards, gives Z-O-D-I-A-C. The whole clue also describes the answer: astrologers draw it as a circle divided into twelve houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac is a circular band of the heavens split into twelve signs, which astrologers call houses.

clue.text: Secret sleepers kind at first in providing material

parts.note: moles are spies planted to lie dormant, sleepers

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of kind
taken as written

explanation.surface: Undercover spies being kind and supplying the goods.
explanation.walkthrough: In espionage a sleeper or mole is an agent who stays hidden for years before acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Moleskin is a heavy brushed cotton fabric used for trousers, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Course includes bread and Irish cheese

indicators.note: including something means holding it within, so the next pieces sit inside

parts.note: a lane is a course, as on a running track
bread is slang for money, cash
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A meal course that features bread with Irish cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is money slang here, not food, and 'course' is a running lane rather than part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is a crumbly English cheese named after the county of north-west England where it is made.

clue.text: Old English county American feller soon takes in

indicators.note: to take in is to swallow or enclose, so the other pieces go inside this one

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
Glos is the abbreviation for Gloucestershire, an English county
an axe fells trees; Americans spell it ax

explanation.surface: An American woodcutter in an old English county will soon be taking something in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' is something that fells, not a chap; Americans spell the tool without the final E. Gloucestershire is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglo-Saxon is the name for the Old English language spoken before the Norman Conquest.

clue.text: Declines travel east, then block books

parts.note: to go is to travel
E is the abbreviation for east
to block is to stop
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to travel east, then has their bookings blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom for deteriorating or falling into ruin, so declines.

clue.text: Duke, as before, comes to court

parts.note: qua is Latin for in the capacity of, as
D is the abbreviation for Duke

explanation.surface: A duke arrives at court, as he did once before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' places QUA ahead of D.
explanation.definitionFit: A quad, short for quadrangle, is an enclosed courtyard in a college, so it is a court.

clue.text: A country boy standing to embrace a spiritual leader

indicators.note: standing up in a down clue means reading from the bottom upwards, so backwards
embracing means holding within the arms, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
Mali is a country in West Africa
a lad is a boy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy from abroad stands up to hug a religious leader.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'standing' turns the first three pieces upside down; only then does the result wrap around the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the head of Tibetan Buddhism, so a spiritual leader.

clue.text: Close to mall, Dame Edna makes purchase

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of mall
Dame Edna Everage was Barry Humphries's comic stage character

explanation.surface: Dame Edna goes shopping near the mall and buys something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' looks like buying, but it is the grip or mechanical advantage sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase can mean a firm hold or mechanical advantage, which is what leverage gives you.

clue.text: Vessel, cutter perhaps, leaving Dartmouth at last

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so a letter goes away from the word

parts.note: a hewer cuts wood or stone; perhaps marks it as an example

indicators.note: 'at last' keeps only the last letter of 'Dartmouth'

parts.note: the final letter of Dartmouth

explanation.surface: A ship, maybe a cutter, finally sailing out of the port of Dartmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'cutter' suggest boats, as Dartmouth is a Devon naval port, but the cutter is a person who hews; drop the H from HEWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug for water, which is a kind of vessel for holding liquid.

clue.text: An oversight, perhaps, Altman's first western not getting Oscar

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective: an oversight is accidental

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the name before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the director's name

indicators.note: not getting something means going without it, so a letter is left out

parts.note: occidental means western
Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: The film director Robert Altman never winning an Oscar for a western was perhaps an oversight.
explanation.walkthrough: OCCIDENTAL drops its O and takes A in front. Altman really did get only an honorary Oscar, which makes the surface ring true.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight happens by mistake rather than intent, so it is accidental; the 'perhaps' admits the definition is by example.

clue.text: Sultanate, British, and a French island

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for British
une is French for a
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A sultanate described as British and a French island.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small oil-rich state on Borneo ruled by a sultan, so a sultanate.

clue.text: Lover one's ditched for a time finds comfortable pad

indicators.note: ditching one thing for another means swapping it out and putting the other in its place

parts.note: a mistress is a lover
one is I, so one's is I plus S
A as written, plus T for time

explanation.surface: A spurned lover is dumped for a while and ends up in a cosy flat.
explanation.walkthrough: In MISTRESS the IS is swapped for AT. 'Pad' is slang for a home, but here it is the padded thing you sleep on.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress is a thick stuffed pad laid on a bed to make it comfortable to sleep on.

clue.text: Weighty pack for climbing soldiers

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means going from the bottom up, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to jam is to pack tightly
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers carry a heavy pack for mountain climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword shorthand for ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Major means of great importance or seriousness, which is what weighty means figuratively.

clue.text: Person from mountainous territory: Alpine ground

indicators.note: something ground has been crushed up, so its letters are broken and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountain dweller on Alpine terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alpine ground' reads as a phrase about mountain terrain, which fits the definition so well that the anagram hides in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nepali is a native of Nepal, a Himalayan country of high peaks.

clue.text: Ship loads drink that's raised in strength

indicators.note: raising it in a down clue lifts it upward, so the word reads backwards
loading means putting cargo into something, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: tea is a drink
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: A ship takes on board drink that has been raised in strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised in strength' reads as a stronger brew, but 'in' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or advantage, a strength in someone's favour.

clue.text: With eschewing personal benefit, no energy for task

indicators.note: eschewing means steering clear of, so that letter is kept out of the word

parts.note: your own things are personal ones
W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: no means without, so the following letter is taken away

parts.note: use means benefit, as in of no use
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Turning down any personal gain, someone has no energy left for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personal benefit' reads as one phrase but splits into two words, each losing a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty placed on someone, so a task they must take on.

clue.text: Varnish Jack's applied to a pot

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
taken as written
a pan is a cooking pot

explanation.surface: A man called Jack glazes a ceramic pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is a hard black lacquer, and to japan is to coat something with that glossy varnish.

clue.text: Scotsman's ecstasy coming into Hebridean isle's elongated bay

indicators.note: coming into a place means going inside it, so these letters are placed within the other word

parts.note: Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides off Scotland
Ian is a typical Scottish name, with the S of the possessive
E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A Scotsman takes drugs on a long bay off a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small island off Mull in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland; the possessive S belongs to the Scotsman, not the isle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ionian Sea is the long arm of the Mediterranean between Greece and southern Italy, so an elongated bay.

clue.text: Servants eschewing foxtrot fraternise improperly

indicators.note: improperly means wrongly done, so the letters are set in a wrong order
to eschew is to avoid, so that letter is kept out of the word

parts.note: Foxtrot is F in the NATO alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Household staff who avoid dancing but get too friendly with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foxtrot' looks like a dance in the surface; it only supplies the F to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Retainers are servants or attendants kept in a noble household, an old word for staff.

clue.text: Partner no longer works, having returned bonus

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: works of art, so art for works

explanation.surface: A former partner has stopped working and came back for a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: EX, then ART backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is something added on top of the usual, so a bonus.
